posts.comment:

posts.caption:
Beat 1: **Studios dismissed her as a lightweight TV comedy star, then she swept two Best Actress Academy Awards.**

Beat 2: Born November 6, 1946, Sally Field celebrates her milestone 80th birthday today, hailing from Pasadena, California.

Beat 3: Pigeonholed into silly sixties sitcoms like The Flying Nun, she fought fierce Hollywood sexism that claimed television actresses had no dramatic weight.

Beat 4: She spent years studying at the Actors Studio under Lee Strasberg, taking radical psychological risks in the harrowing miniseries Sybil.

Beat 5: Norma Rae and Places in the Heart made her a two-time Best Actress Oscar winner, coining the immortal quote: 'You like me!'

Beat 6: She carried the silent trauma of childhood abuse and an illegal teenage abortion, surviving decades of brutal personal turmoil.

Beat 7: From Mrs. Doubtfire and Forrest Gump to Lincoln, she stands as one of the most beloved and awarded matriarchs in Hollywood history.

Beat 8: **Was Norma Rae, Places in the Heart, or Forrest Gump Sally Field's most unforgettable performance?**
posts.comment:
**The secret behind her double Oscar triumph:**
• Overcame industry typecasting by studying method acting at the Actors Studio under Lee Strasberg.
• Won two Best Actress Academy Awards for Norma Rae (1979) and Places in the Heart (1984).
• Received the prestigious SAG Life Achievement Award and Kennedy Center Honors for her six-decade career.

Which movie made you cry harder: Steel Magnolias, Forrest Gump, or Places in the Heart?
posts.reel_script: Pigeonholed in early sitcoms as an airborne nun, Hollywood told this California girl she would never be taken seriously on the big screen. Retraining under Lee Strasberg, she shocked the world in Norma Rae, stepping onto a factory worktable to make cinema history. Two Oscars later, she is one of our greatest living treasures. What was her most unforgettable line?
posts.reel_caption: Did you know Sally Field was told she wasn't good enough for movies after The Flying Nun, then won two Oscars for Best Actress? Her resilience is inspiring. What was her best film? #SallyField #NormaRae #ForrestGump
